title: ProdOps GPS — Runway Guide & Adoption Threshold Catalog
body:
Purpose:
This is a working ProdOps reference that frames launch readiness as a piloting exercise — the "Runway GPS" — combining roadmap milestones, metric thresholds, and action-oriented checklists to decide when to progress between rollout phases. Primary audience: product-ops, release leads, SRE, and the Platform owners for Dedicated/Hosted.

Summary (one-liner):
A lightweight, decision-ready roster that maps traffic forecasts and metric gates to discrete rollout phases (Taxi, Takeoff, Climb, Cruise) and prescribes immediate mitigations and owners for common failure modes.

How to use this doc:
- Use during go/no-go reviews.
- Keep one canonical copy in Drive; link to Confluence ticket PRODOPS-GPS-1 for postmortems.
- Update metric queries (Prometheus/Grafana or internal telemetry) referenced below before each gate review.

Runway phases (definitions):
- Taxi (internal beta): <10k requests/day, used by internal teams + 3 alpha customers. Goal: stability and feature validation with minimal noise.
- Takeoff (private beta): 10k–100k requests/day. Goal: validate autoscaling, model variants, cache hit rates, and billing telemetry under real customer patterns.
- Climb (limited public): 100k–1M requests/day. Goal: validate cost curves, routing policies, and fallback behavior across regions.
- Cruise (general availability): >1M requests/day. Goal: maintain SLOs at scale with standard ops cadence.

Core metric catalog (measured daily, 1h/24h windows):
- Latency p50/p95/p99 (in ms) per route and per model variant. Query: telemetry.latency{route="/v1/generate"}.
- Cost per 1k tokens (USD) by model variant and region (derived from token_count * cost_rate).
- Error rate (5xx + model-failure codes) per 1k requests. Trigger if >1% sustained for 30m.
- Cache hit ratio (prefix/KV) by workload cohort. Goal: >40% in low-latency use cases.
- Autoscale breach count (failed scale events) in last 24h.
- Regression score on guardrail prompts (quality checks) — mean delta vs baseline prompts.

Adoption thresholds catalog (gating rules to move phases):
- Taxi -> Takeoff (criteria must be met for 72h continuous):
  - p95 latency <= 400ms for primary routes.
  - Error rate < 0.5% sustained.
  - Cache hit ratio >= 25% for targeted workflows.
  - Billing pipeline validated: end-to-end rate-limiting + quota enforcement tests green.
  - 2 runbooks written and staff trained (oncall runbook + rollback plan).

- Takeoff -> Climb (criteria for 7 days):
  - p95 latency <= 350ms on average routes; p99 under 900ms.
  - Error rate < 0.3% with known mitigations for transient spikes.
  - Cost per 1k tokens consistent with forecasts within +/-10%.
  - Autoscaling success rate >= 98% on planned spikes.
  - Quality regression score < 3% vs baseline on the seeded prompt set.

- Climb -> Cruise (criteria for 14 days):
  - SLO attainment: 99.9% availability on primary routes.
  - Latency p95 <= 300ms and p99 <= 700ms across regions.
  - Cost/unit at expected commit levels (dedicated vs hosted) and documented pricing adjustments.
  - Disaster recovery test passed (regional failover + model fallback).
  - Support & CS playbooks finalized and paging cadence established.

Rollout gating checklist (for each phase transition — quick yes/no):
- Telemetry: relevant dashboards updated and alerts created (owner: SRE).
- Billing & Quotas: smoke-test validated and customer quota ledger updated (owner: Billing).
- Security & Compliance: dataflow validation + KMS checks green (owner: Security Eng).
- Observability: token-level cost breakdown available in Console (owner: Product-Console).
- Stakeholders: sales/CS notified; customer cohort list approved for traffic ramp (owner: Solutions Eng).
- Communication: launch announcement draft + support notes prepared (owner: Comms).

Quick incident playbook snippets (to keep in runbooks):
- High p99 latency spike:
  1) Confirm scope via example request ids (SRE).
  2) Check autoscale logs for throttle or OOM (Infra).
  3) If autoscale failed: switch to lower-cost routing policy or model variant with documented fallback (Platform).
  4) Temp throttle non-critical routes and increase capacity reservation for primary tenant (Product Ops + Infra).
  5) Postmortem owner assigned within 24h.

- Quality regression (guardrail failures):
  1) Re-run seeded prompt set against current and previous model.
  2) If degradation > threshold, revert to last good model variant and pause canary traffic.
  3) Notify Research/Model-Onboarding and tag PR for urgent triage.

Telemetry queries & dashboards to verify before gate review:
- Latency heatmap: telemetry.latency by route->{p50,p95,p99}.
- Cost curve: billing.tokens_by_model (daily) + cost_rate_lookup.
- Cache analysis: cache.hits / cache.requests by workload cohort.
- Error breakdown: errors.count by code -> surface top 5 failure types.
- Autoscale: autoscaler.events{status!\="ok"} count over 1h windows.

Ownership matrix (short):
- Product Ops: overall gate reviewer, runbook owner, traffic forecast author.
- SRE/Infra: telemetry, autoscale, incident lead.
- Platform Eng: routing/fallback, model variant toggles.
- Research/Applied ML: quality regressions, model rollbacks.
- Billing: quota/rate limiting validation.
- Solutions Eng / CS: early adopter coordination & customer-specific limits.

Roadmap tracker (milestones to keep in sync with roadmap board):
- M1 (Week 0–2): Internal beta kickoff (Taxi) + telemetry baseline.
- M2 (Week 3–6): Private beta (Takeoff) — autoscale stress & cost profiling.
- M3 (Week 7–12): Limited public traffic (Climb) — cross-region checks + DR test.
- M4 (Week 13+): GA (Cruise) readiness + retention of post-launch monitoring.

Weekly checklist for launch week (to be run by product-ops lead):
- Monday: confirm dashboards and alerts, dry-run escalation call scheduled.
- Tuesday: billing & quotas smoke test, CFO/Finance signoff on pricing notes.
- Wednesday: security checklist sign-off + KMS test.
- Thursday: CS & Solutions run tabletop, support playbooks rehearsed.
- Friday: final gate review, signoff sheet populated, comms ready.

Open questions / decisions (TODOs):
- Should we require cache hit ratio >= 40% for Takeoff in caching-heavy customers? (owner: Liam)
- Formalize regression threshold (current target: 3% delta). Need stakeholder alignment with ML Research.
- Add explicit throttling policy for third-party integrations (owner: Billing).

References & artifacts:
- Confluence page: PRODOPS-GPS-1 (canonical runbook + postmortems).
- Jira epic: POPS-987 (rollout epic).
- PRs: platform #4123 (routing fallback), console #298 (cost breakdown UI).

Notes to self (scratch):
- Keep this doc minimal; heavy tables live in the attached spreadsheet (linked from Confluence).
- For the upcoming Takeoff, coordinate a mock failover during low-traffic window (Wed 02:00 PT).

Change log:
- 2024-09-12 created (initial pilot checklist).
- 2024-10-07 added adoption thresholds and incident snippets after tabletop.
- 2024-11-03 clarified Climb->Cruise DR test requirements and updated owners.

If you're reading this during a gate review: pull the 24h telemetry snapshot, run the gating checklist, and annotate decisions in the Confluence signoff (PRODOPS-GPS-1).

-- Maya T., Product Ops
